A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TensorAR, despite the changed title, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither contains appendix pages. However, v2 explicitly refers to appendix pseudocode and additional visualizations that are absent from the supplied file, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, component ablations and refinement visualizations in Tables 3–4 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet experiments, GenEval and DPG-Bench evaluations, ablations and qualitative comparisons in Tables 2–6 and Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: The training corruption procedure changes substantially. v1 mixes input and random-token embeddings and maps the result back to a codebook token through cosine similarity (Equation 4, Algorithm 2). v2 instead specifies categorical corruption with uniform token resampling (Equation 4). Overlapping next-tensor prediction and the residual input/output modules remain.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditional generation on ImageNet and leaves text conditioning for future work. v2 retains ImageNet and adds text-to-image instruction-following and compositional evaluations on GenEval and DPG-Bench. Figure 7 also identifies BLIP3o data as contributing to the text-to-image results.

E2.justification: The ImageNet comparison adds DART and omits v1's GAN/diffusion comparison groups, MonoFormer and RAR configurations. New text-to-image tables compare against methods including Emu3-Gen, DALL-E 3 and SD3-Medium, alongside LlamaGen and Janus-Pro-7B baselines. The training-curve comparison replaces Open-MAGVIT2-B with LlamaGEN-L, and Figure 8 adds a fine-tuned Janus-Pro comparison.

E3.justification: The stated defaults change from two-layer input/output modules and sine scheduling in v1 Section 4.1 to single-layer modules and exponential scheduling in v2 Section 4.1.1. Comparator configurations also change, including MAR from 479M to 943M parameters and VAR from 600M to 2.0B. New GenEval/DPG-Bench evaluation protocols and depth-ablation latency measurements broaden the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 revises the matched-training control curves, adds latency to the depth analysis, and introduces class-conditional and text-conditional qualitative baseline comparisons. The main refinement study changes from LlamaGEN-XXL with k=8 to Janus-Pro-7B with k=4 and a fine-tuned control. v1's residual-design and continuous-versus-discrete-noise ablations are not visible in supplied v2; their possible relocation cannot be checked without the referenced appendix.

E5.justification: Both supplied PDFs report point estimates and training curves without repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty bands, confidence intervals or significance tests. No change in statistical uncertainty reporting is documented.

E6.justification: Many reported results change: LlamaGEN-L-256 plus TensorAR has FID 3.41 in v1 Table 3 and 2.78 in v2 Table 2, under changed method/settings rather than an established identical-setting comparison. The depth ablation's best configuration changes from d=2 to d=1. New v2 results include Janus-Pro-7B versus TensorAR scores of 0.80/0.83 on GenEval and 84.19/85.57 on DPG-Bench. Open-MAGVIT2 quality scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds discrete-diffusion forward/reverse factorizations, categorical transition matrices and a weighted cross-entropy objective in Section 3.1.2. It replaces v1's embedding-based corruption definition with a categorical transition law and introduces an explicit TensorAR training objective in Equation 5. This substantially changes the mathematical formulation, although no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v1's demonstrated contribution concerns class-conditional generation, with text-conditional application proposed as future work. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion claim demonstrated benefits across both tasks, including instruction-following improvements. The central claims of iterative refinement, next-tensor prediction and compatibility with standard autoregressive backbones remain.

C2.justification: v2 Section 3.3 qualifies the full-window diffusion analogy by generation order and adds discussion of local-window scalability, online generation and compatibility with distillation. Figure 7 attributes text-to-image improvements partly to BLIP3o data. v1's explicit ImageNet/class-only limitations are not restated in the conclusion, while the central refinement interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents padding-loss exclusion, cross-attention/MLP module structure and A100 timing that includes generation and VQ decoding. However, v1's pseudocode and detailed optimizer, learning-rate, 20-epoch and 50,000-sample evaluation specifications have no visible counterpart. Because v2 refers to an unavailable appendix containing pseudocode, the full extent of removal versus relocation of reproducibility information cannot be established.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the dedicated autoregressive-language-model history with substantially expanded positioning around masked AR, continuous autoregressive diffusion, discrete diffusion and multimodal generation. It adds a discrete-diffusion related-work subsection and citations including Austin, Hoogeboom, Sahoo and Zheng, while expanding comparisons with DART and newer multimodal models. This goes beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: The title, author information and publication header change, and the abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten. The method is reorganized into preliminaries, overall framework, refinement and noise mechanisms. Experiments gain separate class-to-image and text-to-image sections and more detailed subsections, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The original combined overview and paradigm-comparison table are substantially redesigned into v2 Figures 1 and 3. The model-size plot moves into the introduction and expands to both tasks; throughput and training plots are redrawn. New text-to-image tables and qualitative comparisons are added, and the consolidated ablation table becomes separate scheduling and design tables, including a latency column.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable evidence for previously untested text-to-image applicability and clearer architecture diagrams. However, its promised appendix is unavailable, leaving v1's detailed training recipe and some supporting analyses inaccessible. The new categorical-noise formulation also requires probabilities within [0,1], while the printed default exponential schedule can exceed one (Table 1 and Equation 4). These empirical gains and unresolved reproducibility/formulation problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
